stories.headline: US Envoys Kushner and Witkoff Visit Kyiv for Peace Talks
stories.body:
US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner visited Kyiv for peace talks [c1]. This was their first visit to Kyiv since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine [c1]. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky greeted Witkoff and Kushner at Saint Sophia Cathedral in Kyiv [c3]. On Friday, Russian drones hit the headquarters of Ukraine's security services near that cathedral [c4]. Russian strikes also bombed the two main airports in Kyiv on Friday [c9]. Those strikes forced Kushner and Witkoff to travel to the capital city by train [c9]. They travelled by train because of the risk of Russian drone strikes [c2].

Russia and Ukraine agreed to a short-term pause in air strikes during the visit [c8]. Both countries pledged not to attack each other's capitals over the weekend [c10]. They made this pledge to ensure safe passage for the US envoys [c10]. Before arriving in Ukraine, Kushner and Witkoff spent time in Moscow [c15]. They held three hours of talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Saturday [c15]. Putin told the envoys that Russia was making tangible advances on the battlefield [c6].

After the talks in Moscow, the envoys went to Kyiv [c1, c15]. Witkoff said that peace talks in Ukraine have been very meaningful [c14]. UK National Security Adviser Jonathan Powell joined the talks in Kyiv [c5]. Other European national security advisers also participated in the discussions [c5]. The talks have focused on a 20-point peace plan [c13]. Washington and Kyiv put forward this peace plan in December [c13].

Zelensky said that Ukraine is counting on a winter package from the US and Europe [c11]. He said this package needs to include air defence [c11]. He said it must also include energy support [c11]. He added that the package should include American LNG [c11].

While diplomats met, attacks continued in other areas [c12, c16]. Ukrainian authorities reported on Sunday that at least eight people were killed across the country in the past day [c12]. They reported that 69 people were injured during the same period [c12]. Ukraine also reported that its forces struck the Ryazan oil refinery overnight [c16]. That refinery is about 480 kilometres inside Russia [c16]. The strike caused a fire at the refinery [c16].

Ukrainian officials also made claims about the war in August [c7]. They claimed that Russia suffered 42,000 dead or wounded casualties during August [c7]. They also claimed that Ukraine gained more territory than it lost that month [c7].

vocab.meaning: an industrial plant where crude oil is processed

stories.headline: Amazon Cargo Plane Crashes at Miami Airport Killing At Least Five
stories.body:
An Amazon cargo plane crashed at Miami International Airport on Sunday afternoon, killing at least five people [c17, c19]. Five other people were injured in the crash [c17, c20]. The flight was arriving from San Juan, Puerto Rico [c19]. The Federal Aviation Administration confirmed that 21 Air Flight 7598 overran the runway around 2 pm local time on September 6 [c21]. The aircraft was a Boeing 767-300 cargo plane [c21]. It overshot the runway and struck several vehicles [c17, c19].

Miami-Dade County Mayor Daniella Levine Cava said five people died and five were injured [c20]. More than 60 units from Miami-Dade Fire Rescue responded to the scene [c23]. US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the agency issued a full ground stop in Miami after the crash [c25]. All runways and taxiways at the airport were closed by 3 pm [c22]. The Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office closed NW 67th Avenue between NW 25th Street and NW 36th Street [c24]. Miami Sheriff Rosie Cordero-Stutz said there was no apparent threat to public safety [c18].

The Boeing 767-300 aircraft was over 32 years old [c26]. It first flew in June 1994 as a passenger aircraft [c26]. Cargo carrier 21 Air began operating Boeing 767-300 freighters for Amazon in 2024 [c27].

vocab.meaning: went past the intended landing area
a strip of hard ground where aircraft take off and land

stories.headline: Far-Right AfD Wins Record Share in Saxony-Anhalt Election
stories.body:
The far-right Alternative for Germany party won a record vote share in the Saxony-Anhalt state election [c28]. Incomplete results show the party, known as AfD, set to win 44% of the vote [c28]. Voter turnout in the state was estimated at 78% [c31]. Saxony-Anhalt has a population of 2.1 million people [c30]. Domestic intelligence classifies the state branch of AfD as right-wing extremist [c30]. AfD state leader Ulrich Siegmund called the result sensational [c29].

The conservative CDU finished second with just over 17% of the vote [c32]. CDU national general secretary Franziska Hoppermann called the result very difficult for her party [c37]. She rejected any cooperation with the AfD [c37]. Exit polls showed Die Linke won 9.3% [c33]. The Social Democrats won 8.4%, and the Greens won 8.7% [c33]. The BSW party reached the 5% threshold needed to enter parliament [c34].

Modern Germany has never had a far-right party lead a state government since World War II [c36]. Siegmund promised to launch a remigration and deportation offensive if AfD forms a government [c35]. He also promised to ban rainbow flags in schools [c35]. In addition, he promised to stop new windfarm construction [c35].

vocab.meaning: holding extreme political or religious views
the act of forcing a person to leave a country

stories.headline: US and Iran Exchange Warnings and Attacks in Strait of Hormuz
stories.body:
US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth warned that the United States will sink Iranian oil tankers if Iran attacks American ships [c44]. He said the US will destroy those tankers if Iran shoots at US vessels [c44]. Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said Americans must understand that the rules of the game have changed before it is too late [c43]. The conflict between the countries started on February 28 with US and Israeli attacks on Iran [c40].

Iran claimed it struck an unmanned American vessel near the Strait of Hormuz [c38]. The US denied this claim and called the allegation a total lie [c38]. A report by the New York Times said August was the deadliest month for merchant ships near the Strait of Hormuz since March [c42]. US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said on CNN that about 9 million barrels of oil a day currently pass through the strait [c39].

Wright said on ABC that a nuclear agreement with Iran may not be reached [c41]. He said the US is degrading Iran's ability to develop and deliver nuclear weapons [c46]. In the US, the average price for one gallon of diesel reached $5.85 on Friday [c45].

vocab.meaning: a narrow passage of water connecting two seas
a claim that someone has done something wrong

stories.headline: Anak Krakatau Eruption Disrupts Flights Across Indonesia
stories.body:
Volcanic ash from Mount Anak Krakatau forced officials to suspend over 300 flights at Jakarta's main airport on Sunday [c55]. That airport was Soekarno-Hatta International Airport [c55]. Two new eruptions occurred as the volcano spewed ash across the region [c47]. Indonesian authorities suspended operations at eight airports [c48]. The closures left about 170,000 passengers stranded [c48]. The Indonesian transport ministry reported that 1,558 flights were delayed [c49].

Volcanic ash reached up to 20,000 feet on the Java side [c50]. The ash reached 50,000 feet on the Sumatra side [c50]. Booming sounds from the eruption were heard up to 435 miles or 700 kilometres away [c52]. Indonesia's disaster agency BNPB announced plans for cloud-seeding to wash away the ash [c53]. Port authorities banned ships in the Sunda Strait from going within two miles of the volcano [c54].

Indonesian authorities confirmed that no tsunami warning is active for this eruption [c51]. A previous eruption and collapse of Anak Krakatau in 2018 triggered a tsunami that killed more than 400 people [c56].

vocab.meaning: sudden explosions of ash and lava from a volcano
temporarily stopped or put on hold

stories.headline: Building Collapse Kills At Least Five in Delhi's Satya Niketan
stories.body:
A five-storey building housing college students collapsed in South West Delhi on September 6, 2026 [c57]. The building was located in the Satya Niketan area [c57]. Satya Niketan is a dense hub for paying guest accommodation near Delhi University's South Campus [c59]. Eyewitnesses told local media that up to 50 people were inside the building when it collapsed at around 13:30 local time on Sunday [c72]. At least five people were killed in the disaster [c58, c67]. Reports differed on the number of survivors rescued from the site [c60, c67]. The Hindu reported that 11 people were pulled out and taken to the hospital [c60]. Al Jazeera reported that nine people were rescued [c67].

Residents said the collapsed building was at least 50 years old [c62]. They said the structure comprised a basement plus five upper floors [c62]. The Municipal Corporation of Delhi said the building violated building norms [c65]. Municipal rules permitted only a ground floor plus a first floor [c65]. Repair work was underway in the basement when the collapse happened [c63]. A local shop owner said the leaseholder was conducting excavation work in the basement to expand the hostel [c73].

Police launched legal action against multiple individuals associated with the property [c61, c71]. Delhi Police said they are registering a first information report against Anand Bansal [c61]. Bansal operates the Hostel Daze paying guest accommodation [c61]. Deputy Commissioner of Police Amit Goel said an FIR was registered against building owner Hariram and others at the South Campus police station [c71].

Authorities also took action regarding neighboring properties and ordered an official inquiry [c64, c66]. The Municipal Corporation of Delhi evacuated tenants from an adjoining girls' paying guest building and sealed that property [c66]. Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta ordered a magisterial probe into the collapse [c64].

The collapse sparked student demonstrations in the city [c68]. Around 150 to 200 members of the ABVP student organization protested at Delhi's Civic Centre [c68]. They demonstrated against the Municipal Corporation of Delhi [c68]. A security guard was injured when protesters tried to force their way into the main Civic Centre building [c69]. Delhi Police detained around 15 students after the protest [c70]. Police initiated legal proceedings against them under the Delhi Police Act [c70].

Building safety remains a persistent issue in the Indian capital [c74]. Fire department figures show that more than 1,000 building collapses occurred in Delhi over the past three years [c74]. In April, 11 people were killed when a residential building collapsed in north-eastern Delhi [c75].

vocab.meaning: the process of digging or removing earth
conducted by an official magistrate or authority

stories.headline: ISRO and IN-SPACe Reject Reports of Space Agency Privatisation
stories.body:
The Indian Space Research Organisation rejected reports that it will be privatised or its role reduced [c76]. The agency, known as ISRO, called those reports baseless and incorrect [c76]. IN-SPACe chairman Pawan Goenka said ISRO will remain the bedrock of the space sector and lead next-generation programmes [c77]. ISRO said strategic and nationally critical capabilities will remain under government ownership [c88].

Nine ISRO employee associations sent a joint letter on September 4 to ISRO Chairperson V. Narayanan [c81]. They asked for official clarification on plans to transfer manufacturing to private companies [c81]. The letter was signed by groups including the ISRO Staff Association, SHAR Employees Association, and ISAC Employees Association [c89]. The associations cited remarks by Goenka that ISRO would eventually not manufacture launch vehicles [c82]. They wrote that reducing ISRO to a residual research unit cannot be accepted without debate [c86]. Department of Space employees are organized as service associations rather than trade unions [c84].

India aims to grow its space economy from about $8.4 billion to $44 billion by 2033 [c83]. The country currently has more than 450 space startups [c79]. India targets 50 space launches a year by 2030 [c78]. Space goals include establishing the Bharatiya Antariksh Station by 2035 and sending a crewed mission to the Moon by 2040 [c87]. On September 4, ISRO launched its EOS-05 Earth imaging satellite aboard the GSLV-F17 rocket [c85]. Private company Skyroot launched its Vikram-1 rocket on July 18 [c80].

vocab.meaning: a fundamental principle or solid support
decided or required by a law or statute
